item.title: BE ALERT - YELLOW WARNING - SEVERE THUNDERSTORM - IN EFFECT
item.description:
Severe Thunderstorm/Lightning Warning | Yellow Warning - Severe Thunderstorm - In Effect |

At 5:18 p.m. CDT, a line of severe thunderstorms is located from about 20 km south of Alameda to 15 km northwest of Kelso. These severe thunderstorms are moving east at 40 km/h. Damaging wind gusts, loonie to ping pong ball size hail and heavy rain are possible. Locations and nearby areas that could be impacted include: Manor, Glen Ewen, Alida, Moosomin, Carnduff, Maryfield, McAuley, Storthoaks, Carievale, Antler Golfball size hail has been reported with this storm. Driving conditions will likely be difficult. Heavy rain may cause flash flooding and significant reductions to visibility. Large hail may cause significant damage and injury. Severe thunderstorm warnings are issued when imminent or occurring thunderstorms are expected to produce damaging hail, wind or rain. Severe thunderstorms can produce tornadoes.

| Moderate - possible threat | Immediate - act now | Kenton, Manitoba

item.title: BE ALERT - YELLOW WATCH - SEVERE THUNDERSTORM - IN EFFECT
item.description:
Severe Thunderstorm/Lightning Warning | Yellow Watch - Severe Thunderstorm - In Effect |

A cold front associated with an intensifying low pressure system will combine with an unseasonably warm and unstable atmosphere creating favourable conditions for the development of severe thunderstorms. Thunderstorms are currently ongoing over the region and will continue to grow into a line and move eastward into southwestern Manitoba. The primary hazards with these thunderstorms will be strong wind gusts of 90-100 km/h, large hail, and heavy rainfall. Brief tornadoes are also possible with intense portions in the developing line of thunderstorms. The severe weather threat will diminish once the cold front pushes eastward later this evening. Driving conditions may be difficult. Damage to roofs, fences, branches or soft shelters is possible. Heavy rain can cause flash flooding and significant reductions to visibility. Strong wind gusts can damage trees, buildings and overturn vehicles. Severe thunderstorm watches are issued when conditions are favourable for the development of thunderstorms capable of producing damaging hail, wind or rain. Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to SKstorm@ec.gc.ca, call 1-800-239-0484 or post reports on social media using SKStorm.

| Moderate - possible threat | Expected - act within an hour | Yorkton, Saskatchewan

item.title: BE ALERT - YELLOW WARNING - WIND - IN EFFECT
item.description:
Windstorm Warning | Yellow Warning - Wind - In Effect |

Damaging winds are expected. An intense low pressure system will produce severe westerly wind gusts tomorrow across portions of southern Saskatchewan. What: Westerly wind gusts of 90 to 100 km/h. When: Beginning near noon Monday and persisting until early evening. Where: Portions of southern Saskatchewan. Winds will ease from west to east across the province by early Monday evening. Local utility outages are possible. Driving conditions will likely be difficult. High-sided vehicles will be pushed around by the wind. Damage to roofs, fences, branches or soft shelters is possible. Wind warnings are issued when there is a significant risk of damaging winds. Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to SKstorm@ec.gc.ca, call 1-800-239-0484 or post reports on social media using SKStorm.

| Moderate - possible threat | Future - act in near future | Wapella, Saskatchewan

item.description:
Generic Warning | Yellow Warning - Rainfall - In Effect |

Heavy rain is expected. Heavy rain associated with a low pressure system continues across southern Saskatchewan this evening. Rain will continue through to Monday evening. Rainfall totals are expected to be 50 to 60 mm. Locally higher amounts up to 80 to 100 mm are possible in thunderstorms. Water will likely pool on roads and in low-lying areas. item.title: Premier McLeod on the Enbridge Line 21 Pipeline
item.description:
YELLOWKNIFE - Premier Bob McLeod issued the following statement on the Enbridge Line 21 pipeline today:

“I was pleased to learn that operations have resumed for Enbridge’s Line 21 pipeline after almost 2 years of no activity.

"Resource development has, and will continue to be, the backbone of our economy and is central to ensuring a good source of middle class jobs and business opportunities. Our territory has mineral and petroleum resources and the development of those resources can have a transformative effect on our people and economy.

"Sustainable economic development is key to the future of Northerners. With a strong resource development base, we will be able to support diversification of our local economies into emerging and established sectors.

"On behalf of the Government of the Northwest Territories I’d like to offer my congratulations to Imperial Oil, Enbridge the town of Norman Wells and other partners for getting this pipeline back up and running. I know the efforts and economic impacts of the pipeline have already begun to take shape in the community and will be felt for years to come. ”

 

Charlotte Digness
Media and Communications Coordinator
